_activity: From a 4 to a 5: outside information that reaches
_licence: ORIGINAL, built on the 11.2 casefile documents (numbered per the signed 11.2 map). Quotes are the casefile's adapted text.
design_intent: Not skill practice. A kid here already writes at a 4. This is the gold dust that turns a 4 into a 5: more content, a wider lens, and a named technique.

tidbits.text: Outside information is relevant history you bring that isn't in the documents. It's the exam's own name for it.
Outside information can come from an earlier unit. Magna Carta (1215) and the House of Burgesses (1619) are strong outside information for “no taxation without representation.”
The Threads lane in the Arena is an outside-information bank: every stop is a fact you can bring to a document it connects to.

exemplars.text: Hamilton's argument is supported by Shays' Rebellion, which showed the government was weak.

Hamilton's argument is supported by Shays' Rebellion: in 1786–87, debt-ridden farmers shut down Massachusetts courts, and Congress, with no money for an army and no power to tax, could do nothing. That is exactly the “frail and tottering building” Hamilton describes.
exemplars.what_changed: The 4 names the outside fact. The 5 makes it specific (who, when, where) and ties it back to Hamilton's own words.

techniques.name: Name, date, place
techniques.explanation: Outside information counts when it's specific. “Shays' Rebellion, 1786–87, Massachusetts” beats “a rebellion.”

techniques.name: Borrow from another unit
techniques.explanation: Facts from earlier units are fair game. Reaching back shows you see the whole course, not one unit.

try_it.prompt: Open the Threads lane. Pick one 11.1 stop that echoes something in 11.2 and say how they connect.
try_it.status: Untimed, optional, never scored, never saved — practice reflection only.
